title: Methodology generalisation and the categorical-mass anchor interpretation
html:
Remark. Methodology generalisation and the categorical-mass anchor interpretation

Methodology generalisation

The proof transcribes verbatim to any closed braid K \in B_n whose word factors as \sigma_{i_1}^{k_1} \sigma_{i_2}^{k_2} \cdots with disjoint or commuting generator clusters. Each generator power \sigma_i^{k} reduces via the recurrence (a_k, b_k). We then read the resulting linear combination off the H_n(q) basis. For non-disjoint clusters (e.g., neutron \sigma_1^6 \sigma_2^4 \sigma_1^{-1} with mixed signatures), the same recurrence applies after using \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - h from the Hecke quadratic.

Categorical interpretation

This proposition provides the direct categorical-mass anchor for the proton. The formula \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1^7\sigma_2^4)(q) evaluates the Frobenius integral on H_3(q) applied to the canonical atomic-braid representative of the proton's GB-filtration normal form (prop:atomic-mass-gb-nf). The axiomatic derivation makes the construction independent of any representation-theoretic parameterisation.

The contrast with the Plancherel-trace closed form is strict. The Plancherel trace behaves anti-self-reciprocally under q \leftrightarrow 1/q (prop:markov-trace-antipode-polynomial-symmetry). This Markov-trace closed form does not. The two traces constitute genuinely different categorical objects. Both expand as finite linear combinations of irreducible characters, but they carry different weights (w_\lambda Plancherel vs y_\lambda Jones-Markov, prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price).
